summary:
**Space Relics** is an interactive digital archive that tells the stories of NASA equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. Through a visual, destination-based experience, visitors can explore historic lunar hardware such as the Apollo Lunar Module Descent Stage, Lunar Roving Vehicle and ALSEP experiments, alongside Mars missions including Spirit, Opportunity and InSight.

The project transforms abandoned space equipment from forgotten objects into meaningful pieces of exploration history. Each entry presents its mission background, purpose, status, photographs and timeline, helping users understand why the equipment was sent, what it accomplished and why it remains on another world.

By combining storytelling, NASA imagery and an accessible web interface, Space Relics makes space exploration history easier to discover and appreciate. It highlights how even after a mission ends, the scientific contributions and historical legacy of its equipment continue to matter.
details:
How Space Relics Works

Space Relics is an interactive web-based archive designed to make the history of abandoned NASA equipment on the Moon and Mars easier to explore.

The experience begins with a homepage where visitors can choose between two destinations: the Moon and Mars. Each destination opens an archive of missions and equipment. Visitors can select individual entries to explore their mission stories, descriptions, current status, photographs and historical timelines.

The lunar archive features the Apollo 15 Lunar Module Descent Stage, Lunar Roving Vehicle and Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP). The Mars archive features the Spirit and Opportunity rovers and the InSight lander.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Space Relics helps visitors understand that space missions leave behind more than scientific discoveries. The equipment that remains on other worlds also represents important milestones in human exploration.

The project aims to:

  • Make NASA exploration history more engaging and accessible.
  • Help students and space enthusiasts discover the purpose and achievements of historic equipment.
  • Preserve the stories of equipment that is often overlooked after its mission ends.
  • Encourage curiosity about planetary exploration and the scientific legacy of past missions.

Technology Used

The project was developed using:

  • React.js: To build the interactive user interface and navigation.
  • JavaScript: To manage destination selection, mission information and interactive features.
  • HTML: To structure the website content.
  • CSS: To create the visual design, layout, typography and styling.
  • Vite: For the development environment and production build.
  • NASA resources and imagery: To support the mission stories and visual content.
  • GitHub: For source-code management and project hosting.
  • Vercel: To deploy the website and make it publicly accessible.

No additional hardware was required.

Creativity and Design Considerations

The creative idea behind Space Relics is to treat abandoned space equipment as historical artefacts rather than forgotten machinery. Instead of presenting information as a conventional article or list, the project uses a destination-based archive that lets visitors explore the Moon and Mars separately.

During development, important considerations included clear navigation, readable information, a consistent space-inspired visual identity, meaningful photographs and an organised presentation of mission timelines. The dark, futuristic interface was chosen to complement the subject while keeping the focus on the stories and images.

Space Relics turns the end of a mission into the beginning of another story: the story of what remains.
